title: Problem Overview
content:
Erdős Problem #238: For $c_1, c_2 > 0$, can we find $> c_1 \cdot \log(x)$ consecutive primes $\le x$ with all gaps $> c_2$? Proved for small $c_1$ (Erdős); general case OPEN.

The problem comes from Erdős [Er55c, p.7; Er49c] and was adapted from formal-conjectures (Apache 2.0 License).
mathContext: $\text{mainConjecture}: \forall c_1 > 0, \forall c_2 > 0, \forall^{\!f} x \in \text{atTop}, \exists k > c_1 \cdot \log(x), \exists m, \text{allPrimesLeX}(m,k,x) \wedge \text{allGapsLarge}(m,k,c_2)$.

title: Prime Enumeration and Gaps
content: `nthPrime n` = `Nat.nth Nat.Prime n` gives the $n$-th prime (0-indexed in Lean: $p_0 = 2, p_1 = 3, \ldots$). `primeGap n` = $p_{n+1} - p_n$ is the gap between consecutive primes. Both are `noncomputable` since they rely on the classical enumeration of an infinite decidable set.
mathContext: $\text{nthPrime}(n) = p_n$ via Mathlib's `Nat.nth`. $\text{primeGap}(n) = p_{n+1} - p_n$. By the Prime Number Theorem, $p_n \sim n \ln n$ and the average gap $\sim \ln(p_n)$.

title: Consecutive Prime Sequences and Predicates
content:
Three definitions forming the conjecture's vocabulary:

- `consecutivePrimes m k`: The function $i \mapsto p_{m+i}$ for $i \in \text{Fin}\,k$ — a run of $k$ consecutive primes starting from $p_m$.
- `allPrimesLeX m k x`: Every prime in the run is $\le x$.
- `allGapsLarge m k c₂`: Every gap $p_{m+i+1} - p_{m+i}$ exceeds $c_2$ for $i < k-1$.
mathContext: $\text{allPrimesLeX}(m,k,x) \equiv \forall i \in \text{Fin}\,k,\; p_{m+i} \le x$. $\text{allGapsLarge}(m,k,c_2) \equiv \forall i \in \text{Fin}(k-1),\; c_2 < p_{m+i+1} - p_{m+i}$.

title: The Main Conjecture (OPEN)
content:
`mainConjecture`: For ALL $c_1, c_2 > 0$, eventually there exists a run of $k > c_1 \cdot \log(x)$ consecutive primes $\le x$ with all gaps $> c_2$. Uses `Filter.Eventually` (`∀ᶠ x in atTop`) to express 'for all sufficiently large $x$'.

The double universal quantifier $\forall c_1, \forall c_2$ is what makes this open — Erdős proved it with $\exists c_1$ instead.
mathContext: $\text{mainConjecture} \equiv \forall c_1 > 0,\; \forall c_2 > 0,\; \forall^{\!f} x \in \text{atTop},\; \exists k, m:\; c_1 \log x < k \wedge \text{allPrimesLeX}(m,k,x) \wedge \text{allGapsLarge}(m,k,c_2)$.

title: Negation of the Conjecture
content: `conjectureNegation`: If the conjecture fails, there exist $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that for infinitely many $x$, no run of $c_1 \cdot \log(x)$ consecutive primes $\le x$ has all gaps $> c_2$. This would reveal a structural limitation: prime gaps cannot be simultaneously large along sufficiently long runs.
mathContext: $\text{conjectureNegation} \equiv \exists c_1 > 0,\; \exists c_2 > 0,\; \forall N,\; \exists x > N,\; \forall k, m: c_1 \log x < k \Rightarrow \text{allPrimesLeX} \Rightarrow \neg\text{allGapsLarge}$.

title: Erdős's Partial Result (Axiom)
content:
`erdos_partial_result` (axiom): For any $c_2 > 0$, there exists sufficiently small $c_1 > 0$ (depending on $c_2$) making the conjecture hold. The critical difference from the full conjecture: the quantifier order is $\forall c_2, \exists c_1$ (partial) versus $\forall c_1, \forall c_2$ (full).

This quantifier swap is the entire gap between what's known and what's open.
mathContext: $\text{partial}: \forall c_2 > 0,\; \exists c_1 > 0,\; \forall^{\!f} x,\; \exists k, m: \ldots$ vs $\text{full}: \forall c_1 > 0,\; \forall c_2 > 0,\; \forall^{\!f} x,\; \exists k, m: \ldots$

title: Prime Number Theorem Context
content:
Two axiomatized results providing PNT context:

`average_gap_grows`: For any fixed $c_2 > 0$, eventually some gap near $x$ exceeds $c_2$. This is easy — individual large gaps exist.

`prime_number_theorem_asymptotic`: $\pi(x) / (x / \log x) \to 1$, the classical PNT. This governs the spacing of primes and justifies why the average gap $\sim \log x$ grows without bound.
mathContext: PNT: $\pi(x) \sim x/\log x$, so the average gap near $x$ is $\sim \log x$. For fixed $c_2$, the fraction of gaps $> c_2$ approaches 1, but finding LONG runs of large gaps is the challenge.

title: Run Length Analysis
content:
`maxRunLength x c` = $\sup\{k : \exists m, \text{allPrimesLeX}(m,k,x) \wedge \text{allGapsLarge}(m,k,c)\}$ — the longest run of consecutive primes $\le x$ with all gaps $> c$.

`conjecture_implies_run_growth` (axiom): If the conjecture holds, then $\text{maxRunLength}(x, \lceil c_2 \rceil) > c_1 \cdot \log x$ eventually. This reformulates the conjecture in terms of a single extremal quantity.
mathContext: The conjecture is equivalent to: $\forall c_1, c_2 > 0,\; \text{maxRunLength}(x, c_2) > c_1 \log x$ for large $x$. This means $\text{maxRunLength}(x, c_2) = \omega(\log x)$ for every fixed $c_2$.

title: Large Gaps Eventually Dominate (Proved)
content: `large_gaps_eventually_dominate` (**proved theorem**): For any $c_2 > 0$, eventually some prime gap near $x$ exceeds $c_2$. The proof simply invokes `average_gap_grows`. This is the easy part — individual large gaps exist. The hard part is assembling them into long consecutive runs.
mathContext: This says: $\forall c_2 > 0,\; \forall^{\!f} x,\; \exists n: p_{n+1} \le x \wedge c_2 < p_{n+1} - p_n$. Proved by forwarding to `average_gap_grows`.

title: Cramér's Conjecture (Context)
content: `cramersConjecture`: The largest gap between consecutive primes $\le x$ is $O((\log x)^2)$. This is itself an open conjecture (from 1936), much stronger than needed for Problem 238, but it provides context: if maximal gaps are $(\log x)^2$, most gaps are far smaller, making long runs of large-gap primes plausible.
mathContext: Cramér: $\exists C > 0,\; \forall^{\!f} x,\; \max_{p_{n+1} \le x} (p_{n+1} - p_n) \le C (\log x)^2$. The best unconditional bound is much weaker: $O(x^{0.525})$ (Baker-Harman-Pintz, 2001).

title: Structural Theorems (Both Proved)
content:
Two verified theorems relating the conjecture to its components:

`partial_weaker_than_full` (**proved**): The full conjecture implies Erdős's partial result. Proof: instantiate $c_1 = 1$ in the full conjecture. This confirms the partial result is strictly weaker.

`conjecture_vs_negation` (**proved**): The full conjecture implies $\neg\text{conjectureNegation}$. Proof: unfold `Filter.Eventually`, extract a witness $x_0$, apply the negation's $\forall N, \exists x > N$ to get $x > x_0$, then derive a contradiction from the conjecture giving a valid run while the negation denies it.
mathContext: $\text{mainConjecture} \Rightarrow \forall c_2 > 0, \exists c_1 > 0, \ldots$ (partial) and $\text{mainConjecture} \Rightarrow \neg\text{conjectureNegation}$ (logical duality). Both follow by standard quantifier manipulation.

title: Summary and Status
content:
`erdos_238_summary`: Combines the partial result with `True` (placeholder for the open conjecture). Status: OPEN for general $c_1, c_2 > 0$; SOLVED for small $c_1$.

4 axioms (erdos_partial_result, average_gap_grows, prime_number_theorem_asymptotic, conjecture_implies_run_growth), 3 proved theorems (large_gaps_eventually_dominate, partial_weaker_than_full, conjecture_vs_negation).
